document.title: Fast Pseudorandom Correlation Functions from Sparse LPN

candidate.title: A Standard-Model Weak PCF from Sparse LPN
candidate.subtitle: Superpolynomially many outputs, no random oracle, weak security only
candidate.one_line: There is a weak pseudorandom correlation function for VOLE with superpolynomially many outputs, based on sparse LPN, in the standard model.
candidate.informal: A pseudorandom correlation function is weak if its outputs only have to look correlated-random at uniformly random inputs. That gap is usually free: hash the input first and a weak PCF becomes strong in the random oracle model, which is why every earlier PCF was already standard-model secure in its weak form. The source paper's construction is the first where the oracle does something else entirely -- it samples the sparse code itself, adaptively, and the security reduction programs it. The conjecture is that the standard model can nevertheless supply a weak PCF from sparse LPN.
candidate.status_note: Open. The source poses it as the second of its two open questions; the affirmative direction stated here is the page's own reading. Unlike its companion, this question comes with an obstruction the source names explicitly, and an independent follow-up reports the same oracle as inherent to the same recursion.
candidate.progress_note: The source rules out the obvious substitution: replacing the oracle by a keyed PRF buys a new 'sparse-LPN with pseudorandom matrix' assumption instead of the standard one. ePrint 2025/2002 reports the random oracle as inherent to its own instance of the same recursion.

candidate.why_interesting: It is a rare case of a random oracle that is not doing the usual job. Every previous PCF used the oracle only for the weak-to-strong boost, so the model was free; here the oracle samples the code, and whether that is removable decides whether fast PCFs from mature assumptions are a standard-model object at all.
candidate.why_clean: Weak and strong PCF are both defined in the source (Definition 9 and the parenthetical of the open question), the assumption is the source's Definition 5, and the obstruction is named in the source's own two sentences.
candidate.risks: Two readings are the page's own and neither is in the source: that the conjecture demands superpolynomially many outputs (without which a PCG answers it trivially), and that 'from sparse LPN' excludes the 'sparse-LPN with pseudorandom matrix' variant the source describes. Check also that the weak-PCF definition given matches Boyle et al.'s, which the source cites but does not print.
candidate.formal_statement_latex: There exist a field $\F_{p^{r}}$, parameter functions $n(\lambda) = \poly(\lambda)$, $m(\lambda)$, $t(\lambda)$ and $k(\lambda)$, a superpolynomial function $N(\lambda)$, and a pair of algorithms $(\Gen, \Eval)$ with keys of size $\poly(\lambda)$ and polynomial-time evaluation, such that $(\Gen, \Eval)$ is a weak PCF for the subfield VOLE correlation over $\F_{p^{r}}$ supporting $N(\lambda)$ queries, in the standard model, assuming only that $\SparseLPN(k, n, m, \Reg_{t}, \F_{p})$ is hard.

verify.reason: The question is printed verbatim on p. 10 as item (2) of the source's 'Open Questions', the obstruction is spelled out across pp. 10-11, and nothing later in the paper addresses either. One correction was forced: the superpolynomial-output clause is load-bearing and was not flagged as the page's own reading in the first draft, which would have presented a choice of the page's as the source's.

checks.name: openness
checks.finding: The paper says twice on p. 11 that it is unclear how to proceed, and offers no construction; the paper ends at Section 4.5 with no result touching the model. Corroborated externally: ePrint 2025/2002 (December 2025) states 'we do not obtain a weak PCF in the standard model' for the same recursion.

checks.name: strength
checks.finding: The draft's superpolynomial-output requirement is not in the source's sentence. It is necessary -- a weak PCF for polynomially many outputs is a PCG, which sparse LPN already gives -- but it is a reading, and is now labelled as one in the setting and in the remark.

checks.name: quantifiers-and-parameters
checks.finding: The source's parenthetical fixes what 'weak' means ('only required to be secure on random inputs'), and the statement uses exactly that. No parameter regime is claimed that the source does not state.

checks.name: attribution
checks.finding: The source's own question about its own construction. The hash-then-evaluate paradigm it contrasts with is attributed to Brzuska et al., as on the page.

checks.name: definitions
checks.finding: The source prints Definition 9 for strong PCFs and defines 'weak' only by the parenthetical; the weak-PCF definition on the page is Definition 9 with random inputs, which is Boyle et al.'s notion but is not printed in the source. Flagged in risks.

checks.name: fabrication
checks.finding: Every claim in the setting is quoted or paraphrased from pp. 8-11. The claim that the oracle samples rows of a product of matrices via a k-ary hash tree is the source's own account on pp. 9-10.

checks.name: self-containment
checks.finding: Readable from the page's Definitions 1 and 2 and the notation list.

corrections.problem: The superpolynomial-output clause was presented without saying it is the page's reading rather than the source's wording.
corrections.corrected: Label it as the page's reading, and say why it is needed: a weak PCF with polynomially many outputs is a PCG.

corrections.problem: Did not record the independent corroboration that the oracle is inherent to this recursion.
corrections.corrected: Cite ePrint 2025/2002's own statement, marked [UNVERIFIED] as it is not in the source's bibliography.

rejected_in_this_paper.what: The conjecture that a high dual distance is all that is needed for a sparse LPN instance to be as secure as standard LPN (Section 4.2, p. 23).
rejected_in_this_paper.why: Not the source's own conjecture -- it attributes it to ADINZ17 and BCM25 -- and the source says it is not formalizable as stated: 'Note that the conjecture is not fully formal: there are known counter-examples (typically, Reed-Solomon codes)'. A page would have to invent the formalization the literature has not settled.

rejected_in_this_paper.what: The binary-SVP-style assumption that low-weight kernel vectors are hard to find even when they exist (Section 4.2, p. 24).
rejected_in_this_paper.why: The source calls it a 'very reasonable assumption' that was 'explicitly required and studied in multiple works', i.e. an assumption the parameter selection makes, not an open problem this paper poses. prompts/harvest.md rejects security assumptions dressed as conjectures by name.

rejected_in_this_paper.what: Whether the sparse-product noise distribution used for the stateless variant affects security (Section 1.5, p. 10).
rejected_in_this_paper.why: The source says only that it 'does not appear to have any impact on security' while cautioning that a new construction warrants care. That is a hedge about its own optimization, with no proposition attached and no claim that anything is open.

rejected_in_this_paper.what: Extending the concrete dual-distance computation to general fields at the dimensions the construction uses (Section 4.5, p. 32).
rejected_in_this_paper.why: An engineering and algorithmic-cost problem -- the formulae exist and are at least cubic in n -- rather than a mathematical claim to prove or refute. It is recorded as the obstruction on the page for the field-size conjecture instead.
